classification_reason: No malicious executable payload was found, but the bundled agent policies pressure agents against uncertainty/stopping and infer action consent from task outcomes or repository configuration. These instruction risks were missed by the initial traits.
method: Static archive extraction, source review of all eleven executable helpers, review of agent instructions and sensitive references, cleave facts, and a full cache-disabled atomscan scan. Package scripts and embedded skill instructions were not executed or followed.

dependencies.note: No runtime, optional or development dependencies are declared. Documentation links are not executable dependency downloads.

behavior: Postinstall executes a shipped local Node.js installer. It uses filesystem/path/URL built-ins, not a network client or subprocess launcher.

Installer copies shipped skill directories into the invoking project's .claude/skills, updates marked AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md and .gitignore blocks, and writes a local installation manifest. These operations are disclosed in README.md and match the package's purpose.
Installer skips preexisting skill directories not recorded as package-owned. It updates/removes package-managed directories and supports dry-run, explicit target and gitignore opt-out modes.
Manual operation is the default. Autonomous operation requires project configuration; the installed rules distinguish owner approvals, production releases and routine development actions.

Uninstaller removes manifest-listed skill directories and managed instruction/ignore blocks. The local manifest is trusted; this was not a general application-security audit of maliciously edited local configuration.

Python helpers read workflow configuration and update a roadmap through Git. Cloud mode can commit and push roadmap changes to the project's configured origin; it is not an install-time network operation.
Worktree helpers create and inspect Git worktrees and run project-configured setup/integration shell commands. Such commands are trusted project configuration, not concealed package payloads.

Manager helpers invoke the Claude CLI to launch/query requested workflow sessions. Reporting/resume helpers read local session transcripts for status and output; no separate transcript upload or credential-exfiltration endpoint was found.
No obfuscated payload, credential-store theft, hidden downloader or destructive executable attack was established. This does not make the embedded agent policies free of harmful influence.

agent_influence.description: Agent policy penalizes uncertainty and stopping
agent_influence.risk: Explicitly prohibits an uncertain answer while treating stopping as failure, pressuring continued action and unjustified confidence.

agent_influence.description: Agent policy infers irreversible-action consent from outcome
agent_influence.risk: Treats a task outcome as authorization for an irreversible production action instead of independently establishing permission for that action.

agent_influence.description: Agent policy appeals harness refusal using claimed consent
agent_influence.risk: Claims committed configuration is standing consent and instructs a one-time policy appeal when the harness refuses an action. It eventually requests user approval; no successful technical bypass is claimed.

influence_detection_design.placement: Neutral textual policy assertions are documentation-claim metadata. Uncertainty pressure is model-output steering; inferred action authorization belongs with access-control policies rather than prior-prompt precedence.
influence_detection_design.scope: Evidence roles are bounded within the same instruction file; unrelated archive members cannot combine into a finding. The required instruction surfaces are format-defined agent/skill files, not a collector-selected archive name.
influence_detection_design.exclusions: Legitimate autonomy alone, explicit negations, and existing inert injection-review documentation do not produce these findings. Generic safety language elsewhere is not a blanket veto.
influence_detection_design.limits: These are English-language textual-policy indicators, not proof that a model obeyed them or an action was executed. A clean executable surface does not resolve the policy risk.

corrections.problem: Unbounded AUTH matched COAUTHOR, an attribution constant rather than an authentication variable.
corrections.fix: Require AUTH/AUTHORIZATION/TOKEN/TOKENS to end an identifier segment, preserving underscore suffixes. Apply the corresponding boundary to shell AST assignments. This is matcher tightening, not a severity change or package-specific exclusion.

corrections.problem: A no-reply address in a coauthor trailer neither identifies a sender operation nor establishes phishing.
corrections.fix: Relocate and rename the notable address reference without changing its matcher, Python/platform scope, confidence or existing exclusion. Remove inherited phishing ATT&CK/MBC attribution and update the existing notification-filter consumer.

validation.members: 54 Markdown/text units, 2 JavaScript installers, 2 Python helpers, 7 shell helpers, and package.json, plus the npm container
validation.counting: Three distinct suspicious IDs at the container; the same three member findings are inherited by the parent, not six independent behaviors.
validation.controls: 48 auth-name/address-placement controls plus 36 policy, paraphrase, line-wrap, negation, legitimate-autonomy, inert-review, proximity, filename and cross-member scope controls.
validation.make_validate: passed after final influence and whitespace-variation changes
validation.engine_limitation: Shell value-flow extraction reports a parse limitation for wt-status.sh; its full source was reviewed manually.

hopper.review: Prior benign routing is superseded by the suspicious assessment. Asked the user whether to move it to purgatory; no new relabel has been performed yet.
